note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors; nominations were received on Tuesday 17 May 1955 and Co. Londonderry polled on Thursday 2 June 1955. There were contests in two of the twenty-one divisions, Portstewart Rural and Hervey Hill; 'of the nineteen candidates returned unopposed all but one are former members of the Council' (Londonderry Sentinel, 19 May 1955, p. 4). Council-meeting method: division inferred from the 2 June 1949 return (Sloan B. Kaine; Irish News, 18 May 1949, p. 3); the member spoke at the council meeting of 15 October 1955 and moved the amendment on 5 November 1955 (Irish News, 17 October 1955, p. 3; 7 November 1955, p. 1), about four to five months after the election, as one of the council's elected members (the co-option in October 1955 was for Drumcroon only). The 1958 return has the same member for the division. No other co-option or by-election in the division was found in the 1955 reports read. Returned unopposed.
